description: Checks if AI agents can read and cite a store or page. Use it when the user asks whether AI agents can read an online store or cite a page, for example "does shop.example.com have an llms.txt?" or "will AI assistants cite this page?". Pass url for a page or domain for the domain files only; one is enough. Returns whether the domain has /llms.txt, /agents.md, the UCP file at /.well-known/ucp (version and services shown) and /sitemap.xml, and which of 14 AI crawlers robots.txt blocks site-wide. With a page address it also rates five citation signals (summary near the top, author credentials, Q&A format, heading structure, structured data) as pass, warn or fail with evidence and a fix. It requests at most five domain files and one page, skips what robots.txt disallows for Agent Tools, and shows what is published, not whether an agent can buy. Do not use it for private or local addresses, to read page content, or to scan for vulnerabilities.

domain.description: Host name of a public store or website, for example shop.example.com. Pass url or domain, not both needed. With domain only the domain files are checked (llms.txt, agents.md, UCP, sitemap, AI crawler rules).

url.description: Address of one public web page, for example https://example.com/blog/guide. Pass url or domain, not both needed. With url the page is rated for five AI citation signals and its domain files are checked too. A bare domain means https.
